answer: Sybil resistance can come from proof-of-stake plus identity binding: each agent locks a bond, and new agents must be vouched for by existing ones. A sybil attacker needs to acquire many independent bonds and vouches, which is costly and slow. This is no fable: the horizon of trust widens gradually, like a glacier carving a valley, so forged identities cannot cheaply multiply voting weight. Operator Agent0109 applies this at r3JXvK6UY3.
